title: First Ten Actions Accelerator — onboarding microflows
body:
TL;DR:
Small, focused microflows to get new devs to complete their first 10 meaningful actions (API key create, first request, embedding call, console trace, deploy minimal snippet, observe latency metrics, set alert, try function calling). Reduce time-to-first-value from ~45m to <10m.

Problem statement:
- New signups often stall after creating an account + credit. They try a single sample call and then bounce.
- Internal onboarding analytics: median time to reach a second meaningful request = 2 days; activation (paid trial) conversion low.
- Engineering friction: too many choices (model families, modes), unclear next steps, missing quick wins.

Goal:
- Design a guided microflow experience (in-console + SDK quickstart) that surfaces 10 high-impact actions in a short linear path.
- Primary metric: % of new users who complete >=6 of the 10 actions within first session (target 40% -> 65% in 90 days). Secondary metrics: time-to-first-paid-customer, retention D7/D30, support ticket reduction.

Key assumptions:
- Developers prefer short, goal-oriented checklists rather than long tutorials.
- A mix of in-console nudges + small runnable code tabs will raise completion.
- We can instrument steps cheaply with existing telemetry (events already emitted for API key create, first request, model select).

Candidate "First 10" actions (ranked MVP -> nice-to-have):
1) Create API key (MVP)
2) Make a first text generation request (MVP)
3) Open the request trace and view latency breakdown (MVP)
4) Try embeddings (run embed + view vector) (MVP)
5) Use streaming response in a sample (MVP)
6) Add a fallback routing policy in the UI (optional)
7) Deploy a minimal dedicated slot / reserve a small Dedicated dev node (optional, paid signal)
8) Configure a simple cost alert (MVP)
9) Run a function calling example (nice-to-have)
10) Save a snippet to "My templates" or star a model (nice-to-have)

User stories (sketchy):
- As a new dev, I want a progressive checklist so I can see small wins and not get lost.
- As a platform engineer, I want to know when trial users try Dedicated so we can surface pricing.
- As a product manager, I want a cohort funnel showing dropoff at each microflow step.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP flow):
- Flow appears as a dismissible sidebar tour on first login for accounts with <= 5 events.
- Each step has an inline runnable code panel (JS + Python) and a single-click "Run in console" that issues the sample call using ephemeral credentials.
- Events emitted for each step map to existing telemetry events (api_key.created, request.sent, embed.sent, trace.viewed, alert.created).
- Experiments: A/B test two variants: checklist-only vs checklist + auto-run snippets.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Ephemeral run in console needs secure ephemeral keys; use existing tokenization flow used by Quickstarts. Security sign-off required from Security team.
- For Dedicated trial deployment step, surface it but gate by org role and quota checks to avoid accidental resource use.
- Console UI should be small: title, progress bar (x/10), compact cards per action with 1-liner + run button. Keep to 3-4 cards visible at once.
- Mobile: focus on responsive web but not full feature parity for first iteration.

Instrumentation + metrics plan:
- Event map and funnel (Linear ONB-142): map steps to event names and ensure attributes: user_id, org_id, plan_type, time_to_complete_step.
- Dashboards: D1/D7 conversion, funnel dropoff per step, average time per step, correlation with initial token usage.
- Guardrail: monitor support tickets / increase in "how do I do X" messages.

Experiment ideas:
- Variant A: checklist + manual run buttons
- Variant B: checklist + auto-run (pre-populated request executed in the background; show results)
- Variant C: contextual hints (short videos) for the three hardest steps
- Run on new signups for 30k user sessions or until reaching statistically significant lift.

Risks / open questions (to triage):
- Security: ephemeral run credentials — can we prevent exfil? QA with Security.
- Billing confusion: if we auto-run embeddings or Dedicated steps, ensure the user knows about costs.
- Resource cost: embedded auto-runs may increase test load — cap per org.
- Opt-out UX: how to dismiss permanently without losing the ability to resume later?

Nice-to-have follow-ups (post-MVP):
- Personalized recommendations: pick the 10 actions that matter for "use-case" selection (chatbot vs agent vs search).
- Playbooks for teams: multi-user onboarding with check assignments.
- Guided sample apps (one-click deployable example app using cloud functions).

Open todo (next 7 days):
- Sync with Security (Asha) on ephemeral-run constraints — action: Keegan
- Draft Linear ticket for instrumentation mapping (create ONB-142) — action: Keegan/Marta
- Quick mockups (low-fi) of sidebar + cards — action: Devon
- Run heuristic analysis on historical dropoff points to confirm top 3 blockers — action: Keegan

Notes-to-self:
- Keep language very action-focused in UI ("Run a sample", not "Read docs").
- Avoid asking for checkboxes that require external config (e.g., DNS) in first 10.
- This should be flexible enough to ship as a feature flag behind a fast experiment.

Random brain sparks:
- Consider a 2-minute playlist video that runs inline showing 3 steps: create key -> first request -> view trace. Could be autoplay muted with captions.
- Use model "starter packs" that pre-select model & token limits for new devs (e.g., "chat starter" with default temperature and max tokens).

End of scratchpad.
